title: draw_end commits a stale snap target; surface releases are never re-snapped
evidence:
+func draw_end(screen_pos: Vector2) -> void:
+	if _project_pointer(screen_pos) == Vector3.INF:
+		_snap_target = null
+	if _source != null and _snap_target != null and _snap_target != _source:
+		connect_programmatic(_source, _snap_target)
+	var surface := _project_pointer(screen_pos)
+	if surface == Vector3.INF:
+		return # pointer on the sky — hold the last projection
+| Cancel | Press on node A, drag, release on empty surface (outside every snap radius) | No pipe created; preview disappears | N/A |
detail: Only sky releases clear the snap; surface releases trust the target held from the last on-surface move. After a limb crossing, a release far from every node can still commit, violating the cancel contract.
recommended_fix: In draw_end, re-project the pointer and re-run Geodesic.snap_candidate at the release point; commit only if the release still qualifies.

title: _arc_mid double-scales an already-radius-scaled geodesic midpoint
evidence:
+func _arc_mid(a: NodeSite, b: NodeSite) -> Vector3:
+	var mid := Geodesic.geodesic_points(a.global_position, b.global_position, 2)[1]
+	return mid * WorldSeed.PLANET_RADIUS
+	var radius := a.length()
+		pts[i] = ua.rotated(axis, ang * t) * radius
detail: geodesic_points already returns points at length |a| (~1.01·R); multiplying again by PLANET_RADIUS yields ~64.6. Harmless only because frame_point() normalizes — a landmine for any magnitude-sensitive caller.
recommended_fix: Drop the multiplication; return geodesic_points(a, b, 2)[1] directly since it already sits at surface radius.

title: Comment references a TARGET_ARC constant that does not exist
evidence:
+## The pair whose span is closest to TARGET_ARC — readable in one frame.
+			var diff: float = absf(Geodesic.arc_angle(sites[i].global_position, sites[j].global_position) - 0.65)
detail: No TARGET_ARC constant exists in the diff; 0.65 is a magic literal, duplicated again in test_gesture's _pair_with_arc(sites, 0.65) call. The comment documents a constant never defined.
recommended_fix: Define const TARGET_ARC := 0.65 and use it in both capture_runner.gd and test_gesture.gd.

title: Placement fallback returns a candidate that failed its own separation check
evidence:
+	# Deterministic last resort: FRESH wedge-center candidates (jittered by
+	# the attempt index), still honoring a 50%-of-minimum separation against
+	# everything placed (10 real tries, not 10 re-checks of one point).
+		if ok:
+			return fallback
+	return fallback
detail: If all 10 tries fail, the final return emits the last failing candidate — the comment's separation guarantee is violated, reopening the overlapping-hitbox class the B1 fix addressed.
recommended_fix: On total failure, widen the search or fail loudly; do not silently return a candidate known to violate the separation floor.

title: Preview trestle posts ignore the ghost-preview material and shadow setup
evidence:
+	_preview.cast_shadow = GeometryInstance3D.SHADOW_CASTING_SETTING_OFF
+	mat.transparency = BaseMaterial3D.TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA
+	_rebuild_mesh()
+	_rebuild_trestles()
+func _show_preview(a: Vector3, b: Vector3) -> void:
+	_preview.build(a, b, 1.0, 3)
+		var post := MeshInstance3D.new()
detail: cast_shadow and the translucent material_override apply to the arc mesh only; build() also spawns opaque, shadow-casting trestle posts as children, so the ghost preview renders solid posts while drawing.
recommended_fix: Add a preview flag to PipeArc.build that skips trestles (or disables their shadows and applies the preview material).

title: Geodesic.ray_sphere has no production caller
evidence:
+static func ray_sphere(origin: Vector3, dir: Vector3, center: Vector3, radius: float) -> Vector3:
+	var query := PhysicsRayQueryParameters3D.create(from, from + dir * 200.0, 0b01)
+	var hit := Geodesic.ray_sphere(Vector3(10, 0, 0), Vector3(-1, 0, 0), Vector3.ZERO, R)
detail: The verb's surface projection uses physics raycasts; ray_sphere is exercised only by its own test. The spec code map credits it as surface projection — nothing ships it.
recommended_fix: Either route _project_pointer through ray_sphere (also headless-friendly) or delete the function and its spec mention.

title: Contract test hardcodes snap radius 0.24 instead of SNAP_ARC_RAD
evidence:
+const SNAP_ARC_RAD := 0.24 # ~14° of surface arc — generous
+	var picked := Geodesic.snap_candidate(cursor, [far_node, outside_node, near_node], 0.24)
detail: The test pins a copy of the constant; tuning SNAP_ARC_RAD silently leaves the suite validating the old radius.
recommended_fix: Reference ConnectController.SNAP_ARC_RAD in the test instead of the literal.

title: _empty_surface_point fallback contradicts the file's own unproject-mirror warning
evidence:
+	# Deterministic fallback: the pole opposite the camera (rarely populated).
+	return -cam.global_position.normalized() * WorldSeed.PLANET_RADIUS
+## HORIZONTALLY (around the screen-up axis) — horizontal half-FOV (~38°)
+## clears the limb (asin(R/dist) ≈ 31°) while vertical half-FOV (25°)
+## would mirror an off-screen point back onto the planet.
detail: The antipodal fallback is off-frustum; _unproject mirrors it onto an arbitrary surface point — exactly the pitfall documented nearby — which can land near a node and flip the cancel assertion.
recommended_fix: Make the fallback probe more on-screen directions, or fail the test explicitly instead of returning an unprojectable point.
